items.title: Ozempic may have revealed the brain’s hidden “craving center”
items.summary_raw: Ozempic-like drugs appear to weaken more than hunger—they may also reduce cravings for alcohol and other addictive substances. Scientists are increasingly tracing this effect to the lateral septum, a brain region that helps connect memories and surroundings with rewarding experiences. Packed with GLP-1 receptors, it may act as a crucial control point between thinking about a reward and feeling compelled to pursue it. The discovery could open new approaches to treating addiction as well as obesity.

items.title: The adult brain can repair itself better than scientists thought
items.summary_raw: The adult brain may be far better at repairing itself than scientists once believed. Rather than simply moving into the injured area, these cells perform a remarkable maneuver: they create new nuclei and send them traveling through long cellular extensions to repopulate damaged regions.

items.title: Ordinary WiFi can now identify you with near-perfect accuracy

items.title: Black holes older than the Big Bang could explain dark matter
